subject: humanities
passage: Many older houses in Hyderabad, in the Sindh province of Pakistan, have a tall rooftop structure called a mangh, or wind catcher. Each mangh opens toward the direction from which the region's breeze usually blows. Architectural historian Kamran Soomro argues that builders added these structures mainly to cool the rooms below by directing the breeze down into them.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Soomro's argument?

choices.A: Many of the older houses that have a mangh were built for families of wealthy merchants.
choices.B: Some newer buildings in the city have replaced their mangh with electric fans.
choices.C: When the breeze was blowing, rooms beneath a mangh stayed just as hot as rooms without one.
choices.D: On hot afternoons, rooms under a mangh were several degrees cooler than similar rooms without one.

explanation.why: Soomro argues that the mangh was built to cool the rooms below by channeling the breeze. Measurements showing that rooms under a mangh are cooler than similar rooms without one support the claim that it served this cooling purpose.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Who owned the houses does not show what the mangh was for.
explanation.B: Incorrect. What later buildings did says nothing about whether the original mangh cooled rooms.
explanation.C: Incorrect. If rooms under a mangh were no cooler, the structure would not seem to serve a cooling purpose; this weakens the argument.
explanation.D: Correct. Rooms under a mangh were measurably cooler, which fits the claim that the structure was built to cool them.
